{{Quote|At 0700 yesterday morning, a sociology tour group from the University of Coruscant entered the Temple's public lobby. They then unleashed pre-programmed graffiti-bombs with such messages as 'Broodsnatchers!,' 'Baby Ludi Wants Her Mom,' 'Justice, Peace & Kidnappings' and logos of the People's Inquest movement in the polished interior.|A HoloNet News CoCo District Edition report|<ref name="Activism" />}}
A '''graffiti-bomb''' was a [[Bomb/Legends|bomb]] that used [[Graffiti/Legends|graffiti]] to emblazon images or text upon surfaces. In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], graffiti-bombs were used by twenty [[University of Coruscant/Legends|University of Coruscant]] students to vandalize the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] during a protest over the controversial [["Baby Ludi" custody case]]. The protest was soon stopped by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Judicial/Legends|Judicials]] subsequently arrested the student protesters.

==Description==
A graffiti-bomb was a programmable [[Bomb/Legends|bomb]] that, when released, placed images or text on the surfaces with which the bomb came into contact. [[Graffiti/Legends|Graffiti]]-bombs were used to convey a message or ideal, and using a graffiti-bomb in certain areas could be considered vandalism.<ref name="Activism" />

==History==
{{Quote|The students were loaded into the speeder, by which time the Jedi trance had worn off, and they again became agitated.|A HoloNet News CoCo District Edition report, on the arrests made after the graffiti-bomb incident|<ref name="Activism" />}}
[[File:JediTemple-Deceived.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Sociology students used graffiti-bombs to protest in the Jedi Temple (pictured).]]
In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="Date">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|51|jediwatch/13411_1.html|Activists Deface Jedi Temple Lobby}} is set on the date 13:4:11, which corresponds to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], according to the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]].</ref> twenty sociology students from the [[University of Coruscant/Legends|University of Coruscant]], under the guise of a tour group, infiltrated the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on<ref name="Activism" /> the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="EG">''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''</ref> [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] to hold a protest over the highly controversial [["Baby Ludi" custody case]]. The [[University/Legends|university]] students believed that [[Aris-Del Wari|Ludi Billane]]&mdash;an [[Youngling/Legends|infant]] [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi youngling]]<ref name="Activism" /> that the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] had renamed Aris-Del Wari when she came into their custody<ref name="Inquest">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|46|jediwatch/1337_1.html|Jedi Refuse to Hand Over Baby Ludi}}</ref>&mdash;should be returned to her [[Jonava Billane|mother]]. As a result, the students, upon entering the [[Jedi temple/Legends|Temple's]] public lobby, deployed graffiti-bombs to deface the lobby's interior.<ref name="Activism" />

The bombs displayed several [[Anti-Jedi sentiment/Legends|anti-Jedi]] messages calling for Billane's release from the Jedi Order, as well as the insignia of the [[People's Inquest]] movement,<ref name="Activism" /> a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] watch-group that also wanted Billane to be given back to her [[Parent/Legends|mother]].<ref name="Inquest" /> The protest was eventually ended by the Jedi, and the students were arrested by [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Judicial/Legends|Judicials]] for vandalizing and storming the Jedi Temple. The students' demonstration, including their use of graffiti-bombs, was later reported on in an issue of [[HoloNet News CoCo District Edition]].<ref name="Activism" />

==Behind the scenes==
Graffiti-bombs were mentioned in "Activists Deface Jedi Temple Lobby," an article<ref name="Activism" /> written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and [[Paul Ens]]<ref name="credits">{{HoloNetNewsWeb||credits.html|Credits}}</ref> and published in [[HoloNet News Vol. 531 51|''HoloNet News Vol. 531'' #51]] on the [[HoloNet News (original website)|HoloNet News website]]<ref name="Activism" /> on [[April 11]], [[2002]].<ref name="HNN51 date">{{JCFCite|url=posts/6401165|board=Literature|thread=The Official HoloNetNews Discussion Thread|user=MattPeriolat|date=2002-04-11|time=6:19 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200305125429/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-official-holonetnews-discussion-thread.5990764/page-13}}</ref>
